context:
Goal: the End of mail day view shows what came in today and what is still short.
Problem (rule): a restore from backup stamps every checked line with the restore's time, so right after a restore every envelope with a count reads as checked in today and every short one lands under "Not normal today" until midnight; fixing that needs a second stamp, which changes the saved data's layout, and your rule freezes that layout.
Based on (read): the code review finding of lane hand-end-of-day: the received time is set by the restore code on the phone and by the merge code in the web app.
Based on (ruling): you chose the empty query to open the End of mail day view (item 79 a, 2026-11-19 23:23 CST).
Departs from: main's empty query always shows the start hint — the view shows today's check-ins, and after a restore it counts the restored lines as today's.
Waiting on: your answer; the builder builds option a meanwhile.

lastAnswer.note: on this question, B seems more correct, can you explain this more? is doing B gonna be a lot of work / problem?

options.how: A restore counts as today's check-ins. A debt record notes the gap.
options.label: Accept it: a restore counts as today
options.lose: One noisy day after each restore: every counted envelope reads as checked in today.

options.gain: The view stays true after a restore.
options.how: The view ignores restore stamps and shows only real check-ins, using a second stamp in the saved data.
options.label: Ignore restore stamps
options.lose: A change to the saved data's layout that your frozen-layout rule must allow, plus a stamp the web app does not have.

reply: You chose b, ignore restore stamps (2026-11-21 20:27 CST). Filed in git. It adds a second time stamp to each checked line, optional and defaulted when an older save loads, which the saved-state rule allows; the web app gets it too. The coordinator files the ruling and moves the build from a to b. I close this item when it lands. 20:27 CST.
short: End of mail day after a restore

shown.label: Accept it: a restore counts as today

title: After a restore from backup, may the End of mail day view count every restored line as checked in today?
why: A restore is rare, and ignoring its stamps adds a stamp to the saved data that the web app lacks.
